## What this is for

ad4_21 established that a day's maximum is largely settled by conditions
observable in the morning: dewpoint depression, cloud, rain. But those come
from `weather_observations`, so the desk could only EXPLAIN a day after its
morning had happened. It could not use them to predict tomorrow.

api.weather.gov already forecasts every one of them. This reads the RAW
gridpoint - `/gridpoints/{wfo}/{x},{y}`, not the `/forecast` convenience
endpoint P1.3 uses - which returns about forty time series. AD4 was taking
the temperature out of it and throwing the rest away.

The columns written here are named to MATCH v_city_day_features exactly, so
the model fitted on observed conditions applies to forecast ones with no
translation layer. That is what turns "explain today" into "predict
tomorrow".

## Three unit traps, all handled

The raw gridpoint does NOT speak in the units the observations table uses,
and every one of these would be wrong in a way that still looks plausible:

  skyCover      NWS gives PERCENT (0-100). weather_observations.cloud_cover
                is OKTAS (0-8), because that is what METAR reports. Storing
                a percent in an oktas column would make an overcast day read
                as 100 oktas and every cloud coefficient meaningless.

  quantitativePrecipitation   millimetres. The observed column is INCHES.

  windSpeed     km/h. The observed column is KNOTS.

And `validTime` is an ISO interval, not an instant:
`2026-09-04T12:00:00+00:00/PT6H` means this one value covers SIX HOURS. A
parser that treated it as a single hour would weight a six-hour block the
same as a one-hour block and skew every daily average.
